- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.1), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast at 75–78 for 2–3 periods.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecasts are above 75, adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% per period.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the window; shift forecast down by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.27–0.32 spikes, model tends to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.95 to forecast values.
